- When sentiment is negative and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.  
- When sentiment is positive and forecast is falling, increase forecast slightly to counteract sentiment-driven pessimism.  
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (especially >10% above recent high) should be capped at +5% of prior peak to prevent overcorrection.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above 18-day moving average, reduce by 2–3% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (±0.3+ in last 5 days), reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.  
- If forecast is consistently > true outcome by 2–3% over 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% per day to align with mean reversion.
